ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the side length of square $ABCD$ is $6$. Point $P$ is a movable point on the side $BC$. With $P$ as the right angle vertex and $AP$ as the right angle side, an isosceles right $\triangle APE$ is constructed. $M$ is the midpoint of side $AE$. When point $P$ moves from point $B$ to point $C$, what is the length of the path that point $M$ moves?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram below, connect AC and BD which intersect at point O, connect EC, and draw ET$\perp$BC intersecting the extension line of BC at T.\\
$\because$ $\triangle APE$ is an isosceles right triangle,\\
$\therefore \angle APE=90^\circ$, $AP=PE$\\
$\therefore \angle APB+\angle TPE=90^\circ$.\\
$\because$ Quadrilateral ABCD is a square, ET$\perp$BC,\\
$\therefore \angle ABP=90^\circ$, $\angle PTE=90^\circ$.\\
$\therefore \angle ABP=\angle PTE$, $\angle BAP+\angle APB=90^\circ$.\\
$\therefore \angle BAP=\angle TPE$.\\
$\therefore \triangle ABP\cong \triangle PTE$ (AAS).\\
$\therefore AB=PT$, $PB=ET$.\\
$\because$ Quadrilateral ABCD is a square,\\
$\therefore AB=BC$.\\
$\therefore BC=PT$.\\
$\therefore BC-PC=PT-BC$, that is, PB=CT.\\
$\therefore PB=CT=ET$.\\
$\therefore \angle TEC=\angle TCE=45^\circ$.\\
$\because$ In square ABCD, AC and BD intersect at point O,\\
$\therefore O is the midpoint of AC$, $\angle DBC=45^\circ$.\\
$\therefore \angle DBC=\angle TCE$.\\
$\therefore OD\parallel CE$.\\
$\because$ M is the midpoint of AE,\\
$\therefore$ OM is the median line of $\triangle ACE$.\\
$\therefore OM\parallel CE$.\\
$\therefore$ Point M lies on the line OD.\\
$\because$ Point P moves along side BC,\\
$\therefore$ The trajectory of point M is OD.\\
$\because$ The side length of square ABCD is 6, and AC, BD intersect at point O,\\
$\therefore AB=6$, $AD=6$, O is the midpoint of BD.\\
$\therefore BD=\sqrt{AB^2+AD^2}=6\sqrt{2}$.\\
$\therefore OD=\frac{1}{2}BD=3\sqrt{2}$.\\
Hence, the answer is: $\boxed{3\sqrt{2}}$.
